name: mount
description: Attaches a filesystem (disk, partition, image, network share) to a directory in the tree.

flags.description: Mount a device at a directory.
Filesystem type (ext4, xfs, vfat, ntfs, nfs, cifs).
Options: ro (read-only), rw, noexec, nosuid, umask=, credentials=.
Mount everything in /etc/fstab not yet mounted.
Make a directory visible at another location.

examples.explanation: Mounts the partition sdb1 at /mnt/data — files appear inside that directory until unmounted.
Read-only mount — the safe way to examine a suspect disk without writing to it.
Mounts a Windows/Samba share using a credentials file (username/password kept out of the command line).
Lists all current mounts — /proc, /sys, tmpfs entries are kernel-managed virtual filesystems.

about: Mounting connects a filesystem to the unified tree: everything on Linux is reachable from /. Persistent mounts live in /etc/fstab (or systemd mount units). Modern desktop systems auto-mount removable media via udisks under /media/USER/. Mount options control security: noexec stops binaries executing from data partitions, nosuid ignores setuid bits.
useCases: Mount ISO images: mount -o loop image.iso /mnt/iso.
mistakes: Mounting over a non-empty directory — its contents are hidden until unmounted.
Expecting mount to persist across reboots — add an fstab line or systemd mount unit.
warnings: Always test fstab changes with mount -a (or findmnt --verify) BEFORE rebooting; a bad fstab line can make the system unbootable.
distroNotes: Universal. NFS needs nfs-utils, CIFS needs cifs-utils installed.
